common_name: Abundance Blueberry (High-Yield University of Florida Southern Highbush Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant dormant, container-grown bushes in late winter into acidic, well-drained soil amended with pine bark; Abundance carries a moderate-to-low chill requirement suited to zone 8-10 winters and benefits from a second southern highbush cultivar nearby for heavier cross-pollinated fruit set.

directions: Plant dormant, container-grown bushes in late winter into acidic, well-drained soil amended generously with pine bark or peat, and mulch deeply to keep the shallow root system cool and moist. Abundance is a University of Florida southern highbush release bred for heavy, consistent cropping and a moderate-to-low chill requirement that suits the mild winters of the western Gulf Coast and peninsular Florida alike. The medium-to-large berries are firm and well flavored, holding up well through a home garden's typical multi-week picking window. Though partially self-fruitful, Abundance sets a noticeably heavier crop when interplanted with a second southern highbush cultivar such as Star or Camellia for cross-pollination, and an early-spring feeding with acid-forming fertilizer supports the vigorous new growth the variety is known for.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Southern Highbush Blueberry Cultivars
LSU AgCenter — Blueberry Variety Performance in Louisiana
University of Georgia Cooperative Extension — Blueberry Variety Profiles

common_name: Sebring Blueberry (Very Low-Chill Southern Highbush Blueberry for Deep South Gardens)

planting.note: Set out dormant bushes in winter with good air drainage to protect early blooms from late cold snaps; Sebring's very low chill requirement makes it one of the few southern highbush choices reliable in the warmest pockets of zone 9-10.

directions: Set out dormant bushes in winter into strongly acidic (pH 4.5-5.2), well-drained soil, siting plants where cold air won't pool, since Sebring's very low chill requirement pushes bloom unusually early. Developed by the University of Florida blueberry breeding program, Sebring was selected specifically for the mild, often chill-deficient winters of central and south Florida, making it one of the better southern highbush choices for the warmest pockets of zone 9-10 where many other blueberry cultivars fail to break dormancy reliably. Berries are medium-sized with good flavor, and though partially self-fertile, fruit set improves with a second low-chill southern highbush cultivar planted nearby. Because Sebring flowers so early, protect open blooms from occasional late cold snaps and keep the root zone consistently moist through the Florida dry season.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Southern Highbush Blueberry Cultivars
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Blueberry Breeding Program

common_name: Colossus Blueberry (Large-Fruited University of Florida Southern Highbush Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant in raised, pine-bark-amended rows in late winter; Colossus was released alongside the earlier Optimus for its unusually large, firm fruit and carries a low-to-moderate chill requirement suited to zone 8-10.

directions: Plant in raised beds or mounded rows of acidic, pine-bark-amended soil in full sun, spacing bushes generously to accommodate Colossus's vigorous, upright growth. Released by the University of Florida breeding program alongside the earlier Optimus, Colossus was selected chiefly for its unusually large berry size and firm texture, both of which make it a standout for fresh-market and home use where big, easy-to-pick fruit is prized. It carries a low-to-moderate chill requirement well suited to zone 8-10 winters and shows good field vigor, though cross-pollination with another southern highbush cultivar improves fruit set and berry size further. Prune out the oldest, least productive canes each winter and fertilize lightly with an acid-forming blend in early spring to sustain the large fruit size over successive seasons.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Blueberry Breeding Program
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Southern Highbush Blueberry Cultivars
LSU AgCenter — Blueberry Variety Performance in Louisiana

common_name: Arcadia Blueberry (Early-Leafing Low-Chill Southern Highbush Blueberry)

planting.note: Set dormant bushes with crowns slightly above grade in late winter; Arcadia was bred for reduced-chill winters typical of the Gulf Coast and leafs out reliably even after a mild winter, unlike many higher-chill cultivars.

directions: Amend planting rows with generous pine bark or peat to hold pH near 4.5-5.2, and set dormant bushes in late winter with the crown slightly above grade for good drainage. Arcadia is a University of Florida southern highbush selection bred for reliable production under the reduced winter chill typical of the Gulf Coast and peninsular Florida, combining an early bloom period with good natural leafing so plants aren't left bare and unproductive after a warm winter. Fruit is medium-sized, firm, and well flavored, borne on a moderately vigorous, spreading bush that benefits from a nearby southern highbush pollinizer for a heavier set. Water deeply during dry spells and bud swell, since the fibrous, shallow blueberry root system draws most of its moisture from the top foot of soil.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Southern Highbush Blueberry Cultivars
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Blueberry Breeding Program

common_name: Ventana Strawberry (Early-Fruiting UC Davis Day-Neutral Strawberry)

planting.note: Set plugs or bare-root crowns in fall (October-November) in zone 8-9 for a winter-through-spring harvest; Ventana is day-neutral and flowers regardless of day length, so it does not require the vernalization June-bearing types need.

directions: Set plugs or bare-root crowns at soil level, crown neither buried nor exposed, in fertile, well-drained beds in full sun; in zone 8-9 plant in fall for a winter-through-spring harvest. Ventana is a day-neutral strawberry from the University of California, Davis breeding program, selected for producing an unusually large, early flush of fruit soon after planting compared with older day-neutral types, followed by steady production through the cooler months. Because it flowers on new growth regardless of day length rather than requiring the short days that trigger June-bearing types, Ventana keeps fruiting through a Gulf Coast winter whenever temperatures stay in the 35-85°F range. Feed lightly but regularly through the season to sustain the heavy, near-continuous fruit set, and plan to replace plantings after one to two years as yields decline.
sources: University of California Davis Strawberry Breeding Program
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Day-Neutral Strawberry Variety Comparison for the Gulf South
Louisiana State University AgCenter — Strawberry Variety Recommendations for Louisiana

common_name: Aromas Strawberry (Vigorous UC Davis Day-Neutral Strawberry)

planting.note: Plant crowns in fall in zone 8-9 for a long winter-into-spring picking season; Aromas is day-neutral, heat-tolerant, and vigorous, so thin runners regularly to keep energy directed into fruit.

directions: Plant crowns at proper depth (crown at soil surface, roots fully buried) in raised, well-drained beds in full sun, spacing plants to allow good air movement around the dense foliage. Aromas is a day-neutral strawberry released by the University of California, Davis strawberry breeding program, valued for its large, firm, aromatic berries and strong, vigorous plant habit that tolerates heat better than many older day-neutral varieties. Like other day-neutral types it flowers independent of day length, so in zone 8-9 a fall planting yields a long winter-into-spring picking season rather than the single flush typical of June-bearing strawberries. Mulch with straw to keep fruit clean and off the soil, and thin runners regularly since Aromas's extra foliage vigor can otherwise divert energy away from fruit production.
sources: University of California Davis Strawberry Breeding Program
Clemson Cooperative Extension — Home Garden Strawberries
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Day-Neutral Strawberry Variety Comparison for the Gulf South
